items.title: Ofcom Concedes Defeat in the 4chan Case
items.summary: Article URL: https://prestonbyrne.com/2026/10/20/ofcom-concedes-defeat/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50167028 Points: 100 # Comments: 56
items.content:
Insofar as a political organization like Ofcom is even capable of admitting defeat, it did so in the 4chan enforcement today.

In testimony before the Commons Digital, Culture, Media, and Sport Committee, Ofcom admitted it knows its jurisdiction ends where a foreign court’s jurisdiction begins.

“If foreign courts decide to… try and get in our way, there will be a point at which we have to accept that we won’t be able to recover that money.”

Guido Fawkes characterizes this admission thus: “ Ofcom Admits Defeat .”

Guido is right. American courts have, by now, provided their preliminary view on the likelihood of Ofcom’s enforcement powers being successful in U.S. courts – the obiter dicta in 4chan v. Ofcom , the opinion in the case we filed against Ofcom in the federal District Court for the District of Columbia a little over a year ago.

Those dicta made it awfully clear that Ofcom can expect a very chilly reception in an American courtroom if it ever tries to enforce its fines in the United States. By way of reminder, the Court in 4chan said:

Because Plaintiffs represent that they have “no presence, infrastructure, or operations abroad,” Pls.’ Opp’n at 5; Compl. paras. 20, 24, that likely means enforcing any judgment in the United States. At that point, Plaintiffs could avail themselves of the protection of American courts.

Unless Ofcom is prepared to sail a British invasion fleet here and land ground troops, enforcement would indeed have to proceed through American courts. Which presents the following problem for Ofcom:

American courts generally decline to enforce foreign judgments that violate the United States Constitution , if indeed Plaintiffs are correct in their constitutional claims. See, e.g. , Matusevitch v. Telnikoff , 877 F. Supp. 1, 4 (D.D.C. 1995) (refusing to enforce a British judgment because it contravened the First Amendment and was therefore “repugnant to the public policies of the State of Maryland and the United States”)[.]

Suffice it to say, 4chan’s constitutional arguments are correct.

The Court then added, gratuitously and sua sponte as this was not an issue which was actually briefed by either party in the case,

Finally, at the risk of gilding the lily, to the extent any foreign judgment against Plaintiffs were penal in nature, Plaintiffs may find a receptive audience before American courts regardless of the judgment’s compatibility with the United States Constitution. That is because American courts are not necessarily required to enforce foreign penal judgments[.]

Thus ends that case, for all practical purposes. It would be a gift – to 4chan – if Ofcom decided to show up in an American court after this.

Defeat, for all practical purposes, in one matter, however, will not stop Ofcom and British parliamentarians in their continuing mission to censor the British people, and the world.

What will happen next is that Ofcom is going to go back to Parliament to ask for the authority to obtain “interim business disruption measures” – i.e., more or less unilateral censorship powers to block foreign websites in the UK before starting an enforcement process, rather than after. These powers were explicitly rejected by Parliament the last time around and have even now been repudiated by Nadine Dorries, the former MP who introduced the Bill, having seen what a mess Ofcom has made of it. These powers will also be easily defeated through the use of a VPN.

They may also seek to block 4chan. My client has already priced that in and it is a price worth paying, as this will constitute the UK censoring its own people and ISPs, rather than censoring my client. The UK has the sovereign right to do that. My client has the constitutional right to decline to assist the UK in that terrible work.

The UK thus continues its authoritarian backsliding. Sorting out their own country is, ultimately, a matter for the British, and opposing the grant of new powers for Ofcom – an agency manifestly unable to wield power very well, seeing as they were foiled by a handful of American solos working for free – on domestic policy grounds is a task for the growing UK free speech movement to take up, with urgency.

I wish them luck in that important work. In the meantime, we Americans have plenty more work to do on this side of the pond to protect our border and prevent the British, Australian, Russian , and other foreign censorship regimes from crossing it.

Ofcom has targeted 200-ish American platforms with censorship orders; only four of those sites, all of which are my clients, refused, and only one is 4chan. The First Amendment remains very much under direct, sustained assault from foreign censorship agencies.

We have a long way to go until our fight with the foreign censors is done.

We need permanent U.S. law reform, like passing the GRANITE Act , to turn the tide.

items.title: Jeep Avenger vola a 300.000 ordini: il SUV punta al record della Renegade
items.summary: Jeep Avenger raggiunge 300.000 ordini dal lancio. Il SUV domina il mercato italiano e si rinnova con fari Matrix LED, tecnologia 4xe e nuove dotazioni
items.content:
Che sia un fenomeno commerciale è più che evidente e ce lo ricordano i dati del mercato, che fin dal suo debutto hanno incoronato questo SUV compatto come il preferito dagli italiani. Oggi, Jeep Avenger taglia il traguardo dei trecentomila ordini in poco più di tre anni. La strada però non si interrompe qui, perché l'ambizione è alzare ancora di più l'asticella per puntare alle 610.000 unità della vecchia Renegade in Europa. La distanza da colmare è ampia, ma lo slancio sembra positivo: anche nei primi nove mesi del 2026 la Avenger è in vetta alle classifiche italiane nella sua categoria.

In Italia è davanti a tutti i SUV

I dati elaborati da Dataforce ribadiscono il ruolo centrale della Avenger sul mercato italiano. A settembre il modello ha conquistato la prima posizione tra i SUV, indipendentemente da segmento e motorizzazione, superando il 5% di quota.Come dicevamo, la leadership si estende all'intero periodo gennaio-settembre 2026. Ancora più evidente è il risultato nel competitivo segmento B-SUV, nel quale raggiunge il 10,27% e il 10,92% nel solo mese di settembre. Considerando invece tutte le automobili vendute in Italia, senza distinzioni di categoria, la piccola Jeep si colloca al secondo posto assoluto, con una quota del 2,57%.

Matrix LED e telecamere a 360 gradi

Il recente restyling introdotto a maggio ha portato in dote alcune novità estetiche e tecnologiche, senza snaturare la filosofia che fin dal 2013 caratterizza il modello. Tra i contenuti più interessanti figurano i fari Matrix LED, progettati per migliorare la visibilità notturna, e una telecamera anteriore supplementare che permette di ricostruire sullo schermo centrale una visuale dall'alto a 360 gradi.Il sistema facilita le manovre e permette di osservare gli ostacoli anche durante la guida su percorsi accidentati. Inquadratura e ingrandimento possono essere regolati in modo automatico oppure tramite intervento del conducente. L'abitacolo beneficia di superfici migliorate nella qualità percepita, mentre la carrozzeria introduce le nuove tinte Bamboo e Forest, ispirate alla natura.Restano saldi al loro posto gli elementi tipici del design Jeep: griglia a sette feritoie, protezioni perimetrali, gruppi ottici incassati e sbalzi contenuti. La dotazione comprende inoltre sistemi di assistenza alla guida di Livello 2.

Quattro motorizzazioni

Un ulteriore punto di forza commerciale della Jeep Avenger è la possibilità di scegliere tra più alimentazioni. La gamma comprende varianti: benzina, e-Hybrid, elettrica e 4xe. A seconda della versione si può avere il cambio manuale o l'automatico, mentre la trazione può essere anteriore o integrale.L'elettrica dichiara fino a 400 chilometri di autonomia, mentre la 4xe - quindi la configurazione integrale - combina il motore termico anteriore con un'unità elettrica posteriore, per una potenza complessiva di 145 CV. Quest'ultima consente di affrontare pendenze del 40% sulla ghiaia e del 20% anche senza aderenza sull'asse anteriore, secondo i dati dichiarati dal costruttore. Il sistema Selec-Terrain permette di adattare la risposta della vettura alle condizioni del fondo, affiancato dall'Hill Descent Control.Gli allestimenti della gamma principale sono Longitude, Altitude, Summit e 85° Anniversario; per la 4xe sono previsti Upland, Overland e 85° Anniversario. Con questa offerta, Avenger continua a presidiare un segmento strategico per Jeep, avvicinandosi progressivamente ai risultati commerciali ottenuti dalla Renegade. Il tragitto è ancora lungo, ma il potere di seduzione della piccola Avenger non sembra essersi affatto esaurito.[drivek_widget brand_id="jeep" model_id="avenger-e-hybrid"]

items.title: Apple ha fatto bene i conti con iPhone Duo: massimo due ordini per cliente
items.summary: Apple limita a due unità l'acquisto dell'iPhone Duo per frenare i bagarini, data l'alta domanda.
items.content:
Chi troppo vuole nulla stringe, anche nel caso del nuovo iPhone Duo. Eh già, Apple ha messo un limite agli acquisti di iPhone Duo: due unità per cliente, non uno di più. Provando ad aggiungerne tre al carrello dello store italiano, ecco che il sistema si ferma e mostra un avviso che invita a correggere la quantità prima di procedere al pagamento.

TUTTO VOGLIONO IPHONE DUO, MA APPLE METTE UN FRENO

Il motivo è facile da intuire. I preordini hanno registrato una domanda enorme e, mentre chi vuole acquistare un iPhone Duo per sé deve fare i conti con le attese, c'è già chi prova a sfruttare la situazione per guadagnarci. Su eBay ed anche altri shop online sono comparsi annunci praticamente subito dopo l'apertura delle prenotazioni.

Chi compra oggi direttamente da Apple, invece, potrebbe dover aspettare il 2027 per ricevere il suo iPhone Duo. L'azienda ha ribadito di aver registrato una domanda eccezionale e sta cercando di aumentare le disponibilità. Non è un momento semplice per farlo, anche perché la carenza di memorie sta creando difficoltà ai produttori di tecnologia in diversi settori.

Apple iPhone Duo è disponibile online da Galaxus a 2,369 euro.

items.title: Fino a 1.000 sterline di multa se ascolti musica senza cuffie su treni e bus in UK
items.summary: La campagna Share the journey, not the noise punta a ridurre i rumori molesti sui mezzi britannici con regole e linee guida per treni e bus.
items.content:
Comunque la si pensi, che si appoggi la sua visione politica o meno, Andy Burnham ha ragione. Primo ministro del Regno Unito in carica da pochi mesi, ha rilanciato sui propri social una campagna dalla portata nazionale chiamata Share the journey, not the noise e finalizzata a contrastare una piaga con la quale tutti noi, prima o poi, ci siamo trovati a fare i conti: chi ascolta musica senza cuffie o guarda video a tutto volume sui mezzi del trasporto pubblico. In UK lo chiamano loudcasting.

NIENTE MUSICA SENZA CUFFIE SUI TRASPORTI PUBBLICI UK

Lo ha fatto con il video qui sotto, condiviso sui suoi account, registrato a bordo di un treno per Manchester. L'iniziativa interesserà le ferrovie britanniche e conferirà nuovi poteri alle amministrazioni locali per fare altrettanto sui bus, intervenendo anche sull'utilizzo delle sigarette elettroniche e sull'abbandono dei rifiuti. Sono pratiche che dovrebbero essere regolate dal buon senso, sia chiaro, ancor prima che qualcuno ci imponga un divieto.

items.title: My Friend Bob Cringely
items.summary: Article URL: https://tyma.com/my-cringe-story/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50166794 Points: 71 # Comments: 24
items.content:
In 1996, I was a Ph.D. student at Syracuse University. One evening I was sitting in my office and the phone rang,__ “Hello?” “Is this Paul Tyma?” “Yes?”

Bob replied in very fast English. “This is Bob Cringely. I just read 7 Java books and yours is the best.”

My first thought was “Huh. He actually said my last name correctly”.

But my quick 2nd thought was that there were not, in fact, 7 Java books in existence. I did indeed write a Java book, but to my knowledge, mine was the 2nd on the market and even then, I’m not sure it was the best. My Ph.D. advisor, Doug Lea, had been an early member of the Java project at Sun Microsystems. He introduced Java (and the JVM) to all his grad students and I believe something like 4 of us wrote books piggybacking upon the hype at the time.

In any case, as you might know, it is not common to get accolades or even much attention for writing a programming book 1 . I had no idea who this “Bob Cringely” person was, but, um, Thanks! So glad you liked it - let’s talk some more about how great it is!

I didn’t know it then, but Bob was way ahead of me. It’s likely he pictured me as some lonely computer geek (or “nerd” in his parlance) sitting in a tiny office tip-tapping away at some code enjoying yesterday’s pizza. (He was right). He also knew computer nerds like me were typically a bit starved for attention, especially around anything related to computer-centric achievements. Again, Bob knew his audience.

Writing a programming book in the 1990’s afforded many of the same benefits as today. In other words, nearly nothing. You sure weren’t getting rich off writing books. But it did get me invites to teach Java at some Software Conferences. Which then got me invites to train Java to teams inside different companies. Because of that, my friend and I started a company around Java training. We hadn’t done any contract programming until then, but we’d talked about it plenty.

From there, Bob hired us to build him a system called (or codenamed?) “Pronto”.

Pronto was to be the distribution future of print Magazines. The big idea was for customers (who were paper magazine subscribers) to install a small daemon process on their computer that would monitor for times where their Internet connection (i.e. often dialup modem at this point) was online but mostly idle. Our system would then slowly but persistently download their next month’s issue of “Good Housekeeping” or “Car and Driver””. Once it was fully downloaded, the daemon would lie in wait until 2am the next morning and send the PDF off to their home printer. The customer would wake up to be happily surprised by a fully printed copy of their magazine waiting for them! 2

Like many at the time, Bob didn’t believe that reading online would replace reading a full-color, paper magazine. But how that magazine got to your house could change, and that’s where Pronto came in.

Bob had secured funding for Pronto - from someone in Japan I think. I don’t remember, but I remember Bob paid us consistently for the time it took to develop Pronto. After we finished, I don’t know what happened to Pronto, except that it never released in any meaningful sense. But this did begin my 30-year relationship with Bob (or “Cringe” as we called him).

As I said, before this, I had no idea who Bob was. I didn’t know about his claim-to-fame book “Accidental Empires”. His PBS series “Triumph of the Nerds” was released right around the time I was working with/for him. Well after Pronto somehow I got put on Bob’s list of “People I’m going to send my next startup idea to for thoughts” email list. I was by no means alone on that list, and sometimes I got into email threads with some interesting Tech personalities.

I just took a look - and I have had 320 emails with Bob in the past 13 years. Mind you, those aren’t unique emails, most are part of long email chains so I’d estimate I’d email with Bob about 3 times a year since the late 90’s.

Usually, the email chains started with Bob emailing me a wall-of-text about his new startup idea. While the first half of the email was about the idea, invariably, the 2nd half was about how much money it was going to make. I was always impressed at how “to the penny” he got with his projections for something that was basically an idea written on a virtual napkin.

Some ideas were good, and some were not so good. Through my career, I actually joined him in 2 ventures - home-account and Sonisafe. I have the pitch decks for a few, and the detailed descriptions of a bunch more ideas that maybe no one else has seen. This was a great honor in the beginning, especially as his fame grew. But all along the way, I felt Bob was missing the point.

If you ever met Bob - or heck, just saw him in any of his TV specials, you could see Bob charmed everyone he met. He was good-looking, disarming, and curious. He was also an excellent writer, but it was on the screen he really shined. He was comforting and fun to watch. He was fearless and made people feel special. He wasn’t a “nerd” but if, like me, you were; he understood you and he made it OK. In fact, at times, he even made it look glamorous.

Despite his innumerable gifts, Bob seemed to really want to be a superstar startup founder. I’m sure if one of his startup ideas had exploded, Bob would have filled the role fine. But to me - he was a pure natural in front of the camera. I always thought he should start a Youtube channel interviewing Silicon Valley celebrities. I sent him a few emails along those lines, but Bob would mostly just ignore me. He was usually too excited about his new/current startup idea.

When I lived in San Francisco, he and I had lunch or dinner occasionally. He really was a Silicon Valley celebrity. When the inevitable person(s) would come up to him telling them they were a huge fan, he’d act like it the first time anyone ever recognized him. Every time. The TV Cringe instantly came to life and it was always a pleasure to watch.

Goodbye Mr. Cringely. I’m very sorry to see you go. I will miss you.

Right after the C# language was released (it must have been around 2001 or so?), I spent the evening and into the morning reading about it. Finally around 2am, with bleary eyes and a racing mind I emailed Bob - “Dotnet is going to squish Java”.

I spent the next hour writing an overly long and terribly rough email, in a half-awake, caffeine-induced state and sent it off. I woke up the next morning to Bob’s new blog post - a rather lightly edited version of my rant!

Sharper Than Ever. Microsoft’s C# Language Might Be the Death of Java, but Sun’s the One to Blame

I just remember being grateful he didn’t mention me. But then, he called me later that day, “Sun is a bit unhappy with the blog post. I’ve been summoned to Sun Headquarters tomorrow and you’re coming with me.”

The next day Bob and I went to Sun Microsystems. He and I sat in a room with Jonathan Schwartz (CEO) and Rich Greene (C-something-else) while they defended Java and gave me nasty looks wondering who the hell I was and why the hell I was even there. They seemed plenty interested in impressing Bob though. By the way, Dotnet didn’t squish Java but I did get a Sun t-shirt.

After that, Whenever I emailed him, I often tacked onto the bottom of my emails - “Do whatever you want with this email, but don’t mention me. And know this email could be totally wrong or silly - either way, it’s yours now”.

In and around 2004 I was living in NYC and I got a forwarded email from Bob. It was a forward from a Producer at the TV network VH1 telling him they were doing a video series called “My Coolest Years” and had a special episode about “Geeks” and they needed a computer geek. They asked him if he wanted to be interviewed about what it was like being a “geek” in high school.

“Sorry, but I got laid plenty in high school. However, I have cc’d my friend Paul who actually was a geek in high school. He also lives in NYC.”

I ended up with a total of about 8 minutes in the show alongside Mark Cuban, John Tesh, Ben Stein, and Wil Wheaton. Bob would have been way better.

Randomly, a few months ago I once again watched Bob’s “Plane Crazy.” A classic. And because of the comments surrounding his death I found that his special “The Transformation Age” is also on Youtube which I had never seen (in 8 or so separate videos). It’s quintessential Cringe.

[Bob’s The Transformation Age] (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5FuUcOF0WdQ)

I once did a Book Signing at the SD West conference; I believe in 1998. Mind you, I did a “Book Signing”, not to be confused with a “Books Signing”. I signed one book. I bet that copy is worth something. ↩

We always seemed to ignore the challenges around the idea of having 100 loose-leaf, one-sided pieces of paper that were this month’s issue of their favorite magazine. ↩

items.title: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 73 security recruits, local authorities say
items.summary: Three missiles hit a camp in government-controlled Shabwa province on Monday that was being used as a training centre, Yemen's army says.
items.content:
More than 70 security personnel were killed in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa on Monday, local authorities say.

The Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police.

The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response".

The Houthis' military spokesman said they had targeted "Saudi enemy concentrations".

Yemen's devastating civil war has flared up in recent months.

At the start of October, pro-government forces launched a major offensive that aims to retake territory in western Yemen that is controlled by the Houthis.

With air support from a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states, they managed to regain control of territory on the Red Sea coast that overlooks the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, which the Houthis captured in a surprise assault in September.

However, fierce fighting is continuing there, as well as around the besieged government-controlled city of Taiz, and to the north in Marib and al-Jawf provinces.

The Houthis have also responded to the Saudi air strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in neighbouring Saudi Arabia.

Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says

On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged

'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls

Monday's attack in Shabwa was the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation.

Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces.

A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground at the camp.

Hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and were forced to transfer the most seriously wounded people to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based, Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency.

Shabwa's media office initially reported that 53 people were killed and 200 injured in the attack.

But on Tuesday, it said in a new statement that Governor Awad bin al-Wazir had been informed by an investigative committee that the death toll was now 73, with another 14 individuals reported missing.

Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target.

He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes".

The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers.

In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children.

According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks.

The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August.

In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

items.title: EMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
items.summary: Article URL: https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50166579 Points: 164 # Comments: 68
items.content:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores.

To demonstrate that the keys are compromised, the original reporter Wayne signed the following message with the private key of each of the eight intermediate CAs and reported it to the Root Program Teams on the 17th of October:

proof.zip contains the message, and for each intermediate the certificate, its public key and a signature on the message. To verify with OpenSSL:

The root programs and many downstream trust stores have taken action to protect their users. The certificates have been blocked in Firefox and Chrome since the 17th of October, in Apple devices since the 19th and in Microsoft since the 20th.

The issue was responsibly disclosed to downstream trust stores on the 19th of October. Many have already released updates or are in the process of releasing updates.

An attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs could impersonate any website or service.

This has already been remediated by Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple, and Chrome for their users through their tools for distributing revocation information such as OneCRL , CRLite and CRLSets .

The CA has also revoked the compromised intermediate certificates. However, many other clients do not consume revocation information and require software updates to ensure they no longer trust the compromised intermediates.

A certificate error means the client does not trust the compromised intermediates.

Users should update their browsers and operating systems to the latest versions as soon as possible.

macOS blocks the compromised intermediates, but the built-in /usr/bin/curl verifies certificates against /etc/ssl/cert.pem without checking revocation, and that file has not been updated. To remove the affected roots from it, run as root:

Until a distribution ships an updated ca-certificates package, expert users can distrust the affected roots in the system trust store. This is NOT recommended for ordinary users.

On Fedora, RHEL, CentOS Stream, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and Amazon Linux 2023, run as root:

Please see this thread in Mozilla's dev-security-policy forum.

impacted-intermediates.json lists the eight intermediates and their Sectigo cross-signs. roots.json lists the roots they chain to.

Site published by Dennis Jackson . The source is on GitHub and PRs are welcome.

items.title: 2026 is an exciting year for the Rust compiler (and me)
items.summary: Article URL: https://yoyo-code.com/2026-is-exciting-year-for-rust-compiler-and-me/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50166502 Points: 49 # Comments: 6
items.content:
You might have already noticed that 2026 seems to be a bit special year for Rust compiler. It seems like there's just a lot of stuff going on. Some things were already announced since I started writing this, but there's still a bunch more that's not as visible. I'll share some things that I personally find interesting.

To explain a bit of context, what happened this year is that multiple different initiatives are reaching final steps at the same time. In other words, 2026 is not that special with the amount of work being done, but it's a year when we see several long-term investments starting to pay dividends.

Probably the biggest thing is the next generation trait solver . This is a reimplementation of a big part of the type system, and it has been in the works for a very long time - Almost 10 years in various forms. It fixes a bunch of soundness bugs and unblocks a lot of features and fixes for long-standing issues.

It's easy to understate how big of a deal this is for the compiler. This work resolves a major piece of technical debt that a lot of compiler developers dreamed about for years. It also frees up a bunch of people with a fresh and deep understanding of the type system to work on new things. The queue of things that get unblocked includes many common pain points of the language, even things that might seem benign or unrelated. It contains solutions to big problems in async Rust, or various limitations of impl Trait .

Another big thing is Polonius, a new borrow checker implementation , long time in the making as well. It enables more code to compile and unblocks several related features - including (hopefully one day) internal references. The compiler impact of this is not as big as with the new solver, but it's still a pretty big deal.

My main area of interest is compiler performance, and here we have quite a few things going on. After 1-2 years of a sort of stagnation (at least in terms of results), we suddenly have a lot of things going on at once. So much so that I have a hard time remembering everything, but from the top of my head:

Very old initiative that was put a few years on hiatus with many unclear blockers. The development restarted again a few years ago with a new contributor @SparrowLi , and over time a number of other people contributed to the effort.

Over the years, this turned out to be a massive can of worms. I get the feeling that almost nobody is really happy with the design. However, there doesn't seem to be a better alternative for the foreseeable future, and parallel frontend is highly desirable, so the solution ended up being just grinding through a number of annoying and hairy problems until there's nothing left.

The current project goal is driven by @petrochenkov and is getting close to stabilization.

LLVM 23 was unambiguous and unexpectedly large positive change in performance. For a long time, LLVM upgrades were not particularly great for rustc performance. This changed after LLVM 10 upgrade, which introduced a massive 10% regression, and @nikic , current lead developer of LLVM, called it out in his blog post, Make LLVM fast again . In the post he also introduced a system for tracking LLVM performance over time, inspired by the one we use for rustc .

Since then, LLVM started catching performance regressions earlier, and results for upgrades in rustc went from "less bad", to "somewhat mixed", to "mostly positive with caveats." The last one of those was LLVM 22, which was green on icount benchmarks, but almost universally red on wall time.

LLVM 23 is pretty much entirely positive. I don't follow LLVM development that much, but my understanding is that this is because there's now more work on actually optimizing it, as opposed to working on features without trying to regress performance. These days the improvements come both from new optimizations (those help optimize the compiler during bootstrap) and from LLVM itself getting faster.

Compiler performance has been on a steady streak of improvements in the past few months. There's probably no single explanation for it, just a combination of new contributors coming in, old contributors getting to do more perf work, and tooling improvements combined with architectural cleanups unlocking new opportunities.

With more people working in this area, I've noticed a lot of cross-pollination, where a certain idea would circle around a few people's minds, as people get inspired by each other's PRs and try related things.

I also feel like we got a lot better at managing regressions - triaging and addressing them. This is partially a tooling investment, but also a lot about processes and social structures. A major development here is the connection between tree ops and perf triage, represented notably by @JonathanBrouwer .

This means that people who manage merges often directly triage their performance impact. This is important because it shrinks the response time, but the connection is useful for other reasons as well. The perf impact informs how you group PRs into rollups , for example. Turns out that Conway's law is still a law.

I also greatly enjoy helping people interpreting the measurement results and diagnose regressions. I often find that even just a few sentences from somebody who's been looking at the results every day for many years go a long way towards getting the regression addressed.

All in all, I feel like the compile time concerns are integrated into the development better than they have ever been.

This seemingly came out of nowhere earlier this year, and it's quite interesting. @Amanieu proposed a MIR optimization pass that allows the compiler to eliminate copies that LLVM has trouble optimizing. It speeds up both compile time and runtime.

This is one of those passes that makes sense to implement in MIR instead of LLVM, because the Rust part of the compiler has better information about whether it's valid to apply specifically for Rust. Even more so because it actually requires changing the MIR semantics a bit.

It matters for Rust in particular because Rust typically generates more moves than C(++), which is the primary LLVM target.

This one is particularly close to my heart because I've been following the efforts for a very long time. Polymorphization is one of the most impactful compiler performance optimizations we could ever do, but it's unfortunately really tricky to implement.

This would be the third experiment I'm aware of. This time it's slightly different from the previous ones, and it's inspired by a similar mechanism in Swift.

The difference is that the original polymorphization intends to only avoid duplicate or redundant monomorphizations, so it's purely a compile time optimization with no runtime impact, while the Swift-style one intends to polymorphize everything and pass around layouts of generic parameters as arguments. This will have a runtime cost, so it'll be something you can tweak with compiler flags.

If my understanding is still up to date, next-solver will also enable polymorphization in the previously intended way. Either way, both options run into the same problems, so the work is useful for both. It's also possible that both options come out of this same effort. Either way, this is still just an experiment with a bunch of problems to solve, so we'll have to wait to see how it turns out. The project goal has been proposed and driven by @camelid .

@blyxyas is working on a project goal , which will enable cargo to share artifacts between cargo check and cargo build . The goal is actually more general, but this is probably its most recognizable outcome. This is something we wanted for ages, so it's really cool to see progress on this front.

This was already announced , and it will shrink the target directory size by 5-30%, depending on the workload.

Already announced as well , this is another project that has been in the works for quite some time. As with the other things above, this is major internal restructuring that unlocks other things - namely granular locking of the target directory and cross-workspace caching.

@bjorn3 has been working on fixing support for these two flags, which enable pipelining of build scripts and proc macros. As you can see in the proposal , this is yet another line of work that boils down to fixing a laundry list of internal issues and architectural problems until suddenly a big thing is unlocked.

There have been a number of initiatives in the compiler architecture. I'll mention a few, just to (once again) underscore the point that big things don't happen in big-bang projects coming out of nowhere, but rather as consequences of sustained long-term investments into a healthy system.

Two years ago, @jdonszelmann started the effort to unify and cleanup how attributes are represented and checked in the compiler. Just a few days ago, the last remaining attribute was ported to the new system. This significantly improves how attributes are checked and unblocks improvements to diagnostics and other things.

Earlier this year, @Zalathar and @nnethercote cleaned up the implementation of rustc's query system. This improved performance but more importantly, made the system easier to understand, which was often a blocker for making improvements to it. The system is still a pretty scary part of the codebase, but this is a big step forward.

items.title: Auto termiche in UE anche dopo il 2035: più vicino ulteriore compromesso
items.summary: PPE, S&D e Renew avrebbero raggiunto un’intesa per allentare i futuri limiti sulle emissioni. Il compromesso potrebbe consentire nuove immatricolazioni con motore a combustione anche dopo il 2035, ma l’accordo non è ancora definitivo ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il cosiddetto stop europeo alle nuove auto con motore a combustione dal 2035 potrebbe essere ulteriormente ridimensionato. Nel Parlamento Europeo i negoziatori dei tre principali gruppi centristi – Partito Popolare Europeo, Socialisti e Democratici e Renew Europe – hanno raggiunto nella notte un compromesso sulla revisione dei limiti di emissioni per le nuove automobili.

Secondo un documento visionato dallo Spiegel , la proposta prevede per il 2035 una riduzione delle emissioni allo scarico del 95% rispetto ai livelli del 2021, con la possibilità di scendere a un obiettivo effettivo dell’87,5% attraverso crediti legati all’utilizzo di acciaio prodotto con minori emissioni. Altre ricostruzioni sintetizzano quindi il compromesso proprio come una riduzione dell’87,5%. In entrambi i casi, rispetto all’attuale obiettivo del 100%, resterebbe margine per vendere anche dopo il 2035 alcune nuove auto ibride e con motore a combustione.

Per ora l’intesa riguarda per ora i negoziatori dei tre gruppi politici e dovrà superare diversi passaggi parlamentari prima di poter diventare la posizione ufficiale dell’Europarlamento.

Il primo banco di prova sarà giovedì prossimo, il 22 ottobre, quando le commissioni Trasporti e Industria del Parlamento Europeo dovrebbero esprimersi sul pacchetto. La commissione Ambiente, competente sul dossier, dovrebbe seguirle all’inizio di novembre, mentre il voto dell’intera assemblea è atteso a dicembre. Solo dopo dovrà essere trovata un’intesa anche con gli Stati membri. La normativa segue infatti la procedura legislativa europea ordinaria e la posizione del Parlamento dovrà confrontarsi con quella del Consiglio.

La regola attualmente in vigore continua a prevedere dal 2035 una riduzione del 100% delle emissioni di anidride carbonica allo scarico per le nuove auto e i nuovi furgoni, equivalente a un obiettivo di 0 g/km.

Con l’Automotive Package presentato a dicembre, Bruxelles aveva già proposto di sostituire l’obiettivo del 100% con una riduzione del 90% delle emissioni allo scarico dal 2035. Il restante 10% avrebbe dovuto essere compensato attraverso l’impiego di acciaio europeo a basse emissioni oppure di carburanti come e-fuel e biocarburanti.

La Commissione aveva esplicitamente indicato che questo meccanismo avrebbe consentito di mantenere un ruolo dopo il 2035 non soltanto per ibride plug-in e veicoli dotati di range extender, quindi un motore termico che mantiene la carica della batteria; ma anche per mild hybrid e vetture puramente termiche. Insomma, l'attuale proposta è un ulteriore compromesso della visione originale.

Parallelamente si sta muovendo anche il fronte degli Stati membri. Germania e Francia hanno raggiunto di recente una posizione comune che prevede una riduzione del 90% delle emissioni entro il 2035, senza l’obbligo di compensare integralmente il restante 10% attraverso acciaio verde o combustibili alternativi.

L’accordo tra Berlino e Parigi potrebbe avere un peso rilevante nella costruzione della posizione del Consiglio, anche se sarà comunque necessario raccogliere una maggioranza qualificata tra gli Stati membri.

Francia e Germania stanno negoziando anche su requisiti "Made in Europe", sostegno all’industria locale e accesso agli incentivi, con Parigi particolarmente interessata a rafforzare i criteri legati alla produzione europea.

Comunqu la revisione delle regole sul 2035 è soltanto una parte dell’Automotive Package. La Commissione vuole utilizzare i cosiddetti "super crediti" per favorire le piccole elettriche economiche prodotte in Europa. La nuova categoria riguarda auto lunghe non più di 4,2 metri: vendere questi modelli dovrebbe pesare maggiormente nel calcolo delle emissioni medie della gamma di un costruttore, incentivando così l’arrivo di un maggior numero di veicoli elettrici compatti.

Sono previste anche maggiore flessibilità per gli obiettivi intermedi del 2030 e misure specifiche per i furgoni, settore nel quale la Commissione ha già proposto di ridurre dal 50 al 40% il target di abbattimento delle emissioni previsto per quell’anno. Dal 2030 Bruxelles punta ad accelerare l’elettrificazione delle flotte aziendali attraverso obiettivi nazionali per veicoli a zero e basse emissioni, lasciando poi ai singoli Stati la scelta degli strumenti da utilizzare.

items.title: La Romania ha di nuovo un governo dopo sei mesi di crisi politica
items.summary: Luca Niculescu, il quarto primo ministro nominato dal presidente Nicușor Dan, ha faticosamente ottenuto la fiducia del parlamento
items.content:
Martedì il parlamento romeno ha dato la fiducia a Luca Niculescu per insediare un governo di minoranza, chiudendo così sei mesi di crisi politica. Niculescu è il quarto primo ministro nominato dal presidente europeista Nicușor Dan dall’inizio della crisi. Gli altri tre indicati non erano riusciti a trovare il sostegno sufficiente. Niculescu, che è un diplomatico e ha un profilo tecnico, ha ottenuto 280 voti a favore dal parlamento in seduta comune e 58 contro.

La crisi di governo era iniziata ad aprile , quando i Socialdemocratici (di sinistra ma con posizioni conservatrici su temi sociali) erano usciti dal governo e poi a maggio avevano votato con l’estrema destra dell’Alleanza per l’unità dei romeni (AUR) una mozione di sfiducia all’allora primo ministro Ilie Bolojan, facendo cadere il governo. Sono il partito con più seggi in parlamento e sono stati decisivi perché Niculescu potesse insediarsi. Il governo è sostenuto anche dal Partito Nazional Liberale (PNL) di centrodestra, di cui è leader Bolojan, e dal partito della minoranza ungherese (UDMR).

I Socialdemocratici contestavano a Bolojan l’eccessivo rigore economico e sostenevano di essere disposti a tornare nella vecchia coalizione a patto di cambiare primo ministro. Finora però non si erano messi d’accordo con gli altri partiti. Hanno sostenuto Niculescu ufficialmente per evitare che la crisi si protraesse, ma sono l’unico partito che partecipa direttamente al nuovo governo, con 11 ministri , che per il resto è tecnico. Il PNL ha detto di aver scelto di appoggiarlo per evitare elezioni anticipate che probabilmente sarebbero state vinte da AUR.

Niculescu è un ex giornalista radiofonico e tra il 2016 e il 2022 era stato ambasciatore in Francia, in seguito era stato inviato speciale della Romania per l’OCSE (l’Organizzazione per la cooperazione e lo sviluppo economico, che si occupa di studi e analisi su economia e società). Martedì, durante il dibattito in parlamento, ha rivendicato la sua estrazione: «Oggi sono state usate molte etichette. Non sono un politico, non mi unirò a questa sarabanda di dichiarazioni affilate. Non vi sto chiedendo un assegno in bianco, vi sto chiedendo di capire che alla Romania serve un governo».

Niculescu ha detto che martedì terrà la prima riunione del governo. Il suo obiettivo dichiarato è approvare una legge di bilancio per il 2026 e impostare quella del 2027, con l’obiettivo di ridurre il deficit. I Socialdemocratici hanno posto la condizione che la legge di bilancio di quest’anno sia approvata entro inizio dicembre, e potrebbero esserci nuove tensioni coi partiti che sostengono il governo.

I Socialdemocratici erano stati citati nel caso di Kimberly Guilfoyle , l’ambasciatrice statunitense in Grecia che si è dimessa la settimana scorsa. Guilfoyle aveva sostenuto, probabilmente con una certa esagerazione, che lei e gli Stati Uniti avessero avuto un ruolo nella caduta del governo di Bolojan dopo incontri con dirigenti dei Socialdemocratici. La necessità di avere un governo pienamente funzionante è stata acuita dal moltiplicarsi degli attacchi russi alle navi mercantili nel mar Nero, al largo di Romania e Bulgaria.

items.title: Da Sayf a Nayt a Luchè, i rapper si schierano sugli scontri in piazza
items.summary: Le riflessioni sui social. E Marracash replica: "Esistono molte forme di violenza"
items.content:
Dopo la presa di posizione di Marracash , "con le buone non cambi le cose", altri rapper hanno commentato sui social gli scontri e i disordini avvenuti nel weekend a Milano e in altre città d'Italia.

"Ci dicono che il problema sono le manifestazioni violente, ma chi sta togliendo alle persone il diritto a un futuro dignitoso?", ha scritto Sayf . "La violenza di pochi diventa così il pretesto per delegittimare le ragioni di molti e mentre si punta il dito contro gli scontri si smette di parlare dei motivi che portano le persone in piazza . Si dimentica la violenza di un sistema che mette il profitto sopra la vita e la dignità delle persone, perché il problema non è la divisione tra destra e sinistra, ma quella tra chi sta sopra e chi sta sotto e noi siamo tutti dalla stessa parte: quella di chi sta sotto". Per Nayt, "questa società addomesticata ama l'innocuità, la ricerca e ritrova in tutto quello di cui si nutre, e ogni individuo non vede a più di un metro di distanza da sé . Ma siccome in questo mondo viviamo insieme, a un certo punto, se non vedi l'altro, l'altro ti entrerà in casa per essere visto. Tutto questo finto benessere materiale ha reso borghesi anche i più poveri. Poverini e poveracci". Luchè ha pubblicato una storia Instagram accompagnata dal suo brano Se non ci fosse la rabbia, con le parole: " Non voglio unione / Voglio divisione / Combatto con chi ha / La mia stessa missione".

Guè, Artie 5ive e lo stesso Sayf hanno siglato con i loro like il post di Marracash, oggetto anche di diverse critiche alle quali il rapper della Barona ha risposto sempre via social: "A tutti gli indignati sotto questo post, io dico queste cose da sempre, dalle prime canzoni. Cambiate artista. La violenza va condannata ma anche quando la polizia manganella gli studenti, quando ci sono i caschi senza numero di matricola, lo scudo penale. Per una generazione senza futuro, che studia per niente, distrutta dagli psicofarmaci, messa ai margini davanti a una vetrina di status symbol che non avrà mai e il mantra che sei quello che hai e cioè niente. Esistono molte forme di violenza".

Anche Nerone ha preso posizione : "Milioni di persone in tutta Italia stanno protestando pacificamente per cercare di farsi sentire da sti merda mangiasoldi. Nello stesso momento ma non insieme a loro 400 clown minorenni con le squalo e i buchi nel cervello hanno sfondato negozi e auto come le peggiori delle bestie. Questa porcata è stata strumentalizzata a favore di chi continua a gettare fumo negli occhi alla povera gente . Persone senza risposte che non vedono l'ora di avere un altro problema da non saper risolvere. Nessuno sa risolvere un cazzo qua. Manco io. Ma almeno promesse non ne faccio".

items.title: How I got over 300 Tor exit nodes removed
items.summary: Article URL: https://kaba.cx/posts/20261020_Tor/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50166257 Points: 122 # Comments: 32
items.content:
On Friday Oct 2, 09:35am, 333 infected exit nodes started a coordinated campaign to intercept SSH connections and gather as much unencrypted data as possible.

To give you a sense of scale, all of Tor has around 3000 exit relays, so roughly 10% were under their control.

The attackers had gained access to the servers two months earlier, in August, and quietly deployed their Ebury 1.8.3 payload (an OpenSSH backdoor and credential stealer for Linux).

By blocking certain ports, they made their exit nodes handle only unencrypted mail traffic. An interesting writeup by one of the victims (a veteran Tor operator) goes into great detail about that: lists.torproject.org/mailman3

In this post I'll focus on the second attack, the SSH MITM. If you happen to get a circuit that exits over one of those 333 infected exit nodes, you won't notice anything at first. Encrypted web traffic is forwarded as usual, but if you attempt an SSH connection over Port 22, you're unknowingly redirected to one of 12 SSH interception servers.

That's exactly what happened to me on Friday morning. My SSH connection got redirected, and I was greeted with this warning:

But if you ignore the warning and go ahead with the login, the attacker does three things:

On Friday evening I contacted the Tor Project's network health team with my findings. They confirmed this was something new and got to work by contacting the affected relay operators.

In their announcement, the health team described the pattern:

You can see the impact of those 333 exit nodes being shut down. On metrics.torproject.org a clear dip is visible on October 4th and has not recovered since.

Consider running a relay: community.torproject.org/relay/setup/

In this part I'll go into detail about how I found all the infected exit nodes.

Using exitmap , I built a simple script that did the following: it pinned an exit node, then opened an SSH connection from my server A to my server B.

I ran the script against every single one of the ~3000 exit relays. Around a dozen served a fake fingerprint, and over 300 didn't intercept anything but redirected through those same interception servers. Redirecting alone was enough to confirm the exit was infected.

In some further analysis I used sshesame as a honeypot. Tricking the MITM into logging into the honeypot showed that they used paramiko (a Python SSH library) and also how they attempted to install Ebury using Perl.

Checking for permissions first, then executing a base64-encoded command.

The biggest question is still how they got into all those servers in the first place. One theory is that the hosting company itself was hacked (discussed here: lists.torproject.org ). But that's just a theory floating around. In truth, no one really knows.

Another is who's behind it. The use of Ebury and the broad collection of unencrypted data point to a financially motivated crime group. Though this too is just speculation.

I also suspect they deliberately launched their attack on a Friday, hoping that no one would want to ruin their weekend by responding. All the more credit to the Tor Team for acting so quickly!

The lesson is the same as always: extra security is a worthwhile investment. Disable password authentication in favor of ssh keys. I for one am going to buy myself some hardware keys today. :)

items.title: Google segnala guasti di rete a 'diversi' servizi cloud in Europa. Anche Revolut in tilt
items.summary: Altri istituti di credito down, disagi per gli utenti. Il problema riguarda il centro dati europeo di Google a Londra. Adusbef: 'Subito indennizzi o partiranno azioni legali'
items.content:
Problemi a più servizi cloud di Google in Europa hanno provocato da questa mattina disagi a banche, aziende e servizi online. Il guasto riguarda il centro dati europeo del gruppo a Londra , dove Google Cloud ha confermato "un problema con diversi servizi". "Il nostro team di ingegneri continua a indagare sul problema. Ci scusiamo con tutti coloro che sono colpiti dall'interruzione", si legge in una nota del colosso americano.

Secondo il sito Downdetector, centinaia di segnalazioni di disservizi riguardano le banche britanniche Lloyds, Hsbc e Revolut, il sito immobiliare Rightmove, le poste Royal Mail, il gruppo telefonico Bt e il corriere Dpd .

Il guasto, ha precisato Google, è iniziato di primo mattino, e al momento non se ne conoscono le cause . Migliaia di clienti di Revolut hanno avuto difficoltà a effettuare pagamenti e ad accedere ai propri fondi. Un portavoce ha assicurato che la banca "lavora per risolvere il problema da quando è stato individuato" e ha presentato le sue scuse "a chiunque sia stato colpito e per ogni disagio causato". "Possiamo confermare che il denaro e i dati di tutti i nostri clienti sono al sicuro", ha aggiunto.

"Attualmente stiamo riscontrando un'interruzione che interessa diversi servizi a causa di un guasto recente su Google Cloud. Confermiamo che i fondi e i dati di tutti i nostri clienti sono al sicuro. Stiamo lavorando per risolvere il problema da quando è stato individuato questa mattina e ci scusiamo con tutte le persone coinvolte per l'inconveniente arrecato". E' quanto afferma un portavoce di Revolut Bank, a seguito dell'interruzione dei servizi di un fornitore terzo, Google Cloud, che ha causato disservizi anche per le banche britanniche Lloyds, Hsbc, il sito immobiliare Rightmove, le poste Royal Mail, il gruppo telefonico Bt e il corriere Dpd.

Ancora disagi per i clienti Revolut, con alcuni servizi della banca digitale bloccati da questa mattina. Un disservizio che si aggiunge al caso scoppiato solo lo scorso mese, quando l'azienda è stata vittima di una truffa perpetrata attraverso l'invio di una email istituzionale compromessa che avrebbe portato al furto di dati sensibili dei clienti. Lo afferma Adusbef (associazione Difesa Utenti Servizi Bancari), che chiede alla banca di attivarsi per riconoscere indennizzi automatici in favore degli utenti coinvolti.

"I clienti italiani Revolut stanno subendo oggi pesanti disagi a causa dell'impossibilità di compiere una moltitudine di operazioni come pagamenti, bonifici, prelievi agli sportelli e operazioni online. - spiega il presidente Antonio Tanza - Un disservizio grave che arreca un enorme danno ai cittadini, i quali non riescono a effettuare operazioni basilari come acquisti, invio di denaro o prelievi di denaro contante. Per questo chiediamo alla banca di prevedere un indennizzo automatico in favore di tutti i clienti italiani coinvolti nel disservizio. In caso contrario, Adusbef si mette sin da ora a disposizione degli interessati ai fini delle dovute azioni legali volte ad ottenere il risarcimento dei danni subiti", conclude Tanza.

items.title: Huge setback for Alberta's separatist movement after decisive defeat
items.summary: Leaders of the movement for independence vow to push on but the margin of defeat could make that difficult.
items.content:
It was a decisive result in a referendum that could have strained the bonds of national unity.

But preliminary results show that more than two-thirds of Alberta voters sent a clear message that they want to remain in Canada.

It's possible that once the final tally is counted, the rejection by a comfortable majority of voters to pursue separation through a binding referendum could halt Alberta's separatist sentiment in its tracks.

This would push the idea that had been discussed quietly for decades back into the political fringes.

For leaders of the Alberta separatist movement, while the result was expected given the polling, it was still disappointing after more than a year of campaigning and pushing for a vote on separation.

Asked by the BBC how he felt in one sentence after the results, separatist leader Mitch Sylvestre simply said: "Not happy".

The outcome was celebrated almost immediately by Prime Minister Mark Carney, who said in a statement that "Albertans made a clear choice".

But the movement's leaders say their battle is long from over and that the issue could dominate Alberta politics for years to come.

Jeffrey Rath, a Calgary-lawyer and one of the main spokespeople for Alberta separation, said he and others "plan to roll up our sleeves and work harder".

Keith Wilson, another separatist, told supporters in Calgary that while the vote is over, "the conversation about Alberta's future in Canada and our place in Canada and our role in Canada will continue".

Smith, who openly supported and campaigned for the unity vote, thanked voters for the result.

The Alberta premier has been criticised for taking a "dangerous" gamble that the independence push would likely face defeat while still giving her restive base what they wanted.

She lowered the petition threshold needed to get the citizen-led campaign the ballot in the first place.

How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

Carney pitches oil pipeline as a response to US-Canada trade war

At Canada's biggest rodeo, the starting gun is fired in the fight over Alberta separation

By making Monday's result non-binding, she got around a court decision blocking the pro-separation petition because it failed to consult indigenous First Nations whose land would be affected if the province separated.

That gamble could test her leadership of the United Conservative Party, which she has led since 2022.

Albertans who voted against an independence referendum told the BBC throughout the campaign that they were motivated by a desire to keep the country united, especially as Canada grapples with tariff threats from the US, its longtime ally.

They also feared that an independent Alberta could be vulnerable to outside influence - or even annexation.

Thomas Lukaszuk, a prominent pro-unity campaigner, told a crowd of supporters on Monday night that the early results made him proud to be Albertan.

At a pro-unity results watch party in Edmonton, Lukaszuk appealled directly to separatists, saying that "some of the issues they have raised are legitimate", and that the province must do the hard work of healing the divisions laid bare by this debate.

"I don't want to see us doing another referendum like this ever again," Lukaszuk said.

Premier Smith told CBC earlier in the week that she would not hold an independence referendum if Albertans vote against it as long as she is premier.

The separatist sentiment has its roots in "western alienation" which is a term that has been used for decades by some in Canada's western provinces to describe a feeling of being ignored or overlooked by the federal government in central Canada.

Alberta independence supporters - and many on the unity side - believe that Ottawa has long undermined the province's oil and gas industry, most recently through environmental policies.

That anger later deepened as some Albertans grew frustrated with the response by former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau to the Covid-19 pandemic and vaccine mandates, viewing them as yet another example of government overreach.

Carney, who was raised in Alberta, has worked with Smith to address some of these issues, signing an agreement that would see a new pipeline from Alberta built to Canada's pacific coast.

He nodded to that in his statement on Monday night, saying that his plan is to unlock Canada's "full potential as a global energy superpower with Alberta at its core".

But there are signs that there could be tension in the future between Carney and Smith, an able politician and a survivor - so far - of Alberta's rough and tumble politics.

She also put nine other questions to Albertans on Monday, most that seek to give the province more autonomy from Ottawa, including on matters like immigration.

The (very) preliminary results suggest that many might pass.

Some who voted in favour of a second binding separation referendum have said they didn't want outright independence, but some leverage over Ottawa. Smith has said these other nine questions help give her just that.

Quebec, another province with similar sovereigntist sentiments, could offer clues on where Alberta's separation movement might end up.

They held two separation referendums, in 1980 and 1995, both of which were defeated by a close margin.

Alberta independence supporters don't hide the fact that they gain inspiration from the majority French-speaking province.

They view Quebec as having successfully used the threat of separation to gain significantly more autonomy over provincial affairs.

And despite support for Quebec sovereignty being at historic lows, a newly elected provincial government has pledged to hold a third referendum on independence by 2030.

The sovereigntist Parti Quebecois "has just formed the government of Quebec with 28% of the vote," he said.

"It's not out of the realm of possibility", he added, that Alberta separatists could do the same in the future.

items.title: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
items.summary: Dan Mackenzie initially defended his father but now says he felt he had to report his own grandmother.
items.content:
The eldest son of Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie, convicted of murdering 191 people, says his younger siblings were still being forced to fast as recently as two weeks ago.

Dan Mackenzie, 27, said he reported the case to police, who rescued eight children, including his five younger siblings from their grandmother's house, and took them to a rescue centre.

"They were basically forcibly fasted because they were denying food to them for almost three days," he tells BBC's Newsday.

His father was found guilty on Monday of murdering 190 children and one adult who starved to death in Shakahola forest, near the Kenyan coast.

He had ordered members of his doomsday cult to starve themselves and their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

Twenty-eight other cult leaders were also convicted of murder.

Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders

Dan Mackenzie, who had initially defended his father, said at first he had struggled to understand the allegations against the cult leader, but came to realise the scale of the tragedy during the court proceedings.

"When I was 12, I was forced to fast for almost a week," he says. He also remembers church members beating him for hours to make him attend a service as a child.

Now, he says he felt he had to report family members who still believe in the teachings in order to free his siblings. "I had to report my grandmother."

The cult leader's doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil".

Now living in the coastal town of Malindi, Dan earns a living as a motorcycle taxi driver, supporting himself and his younger siblings.

He said some people in the town had been angry with him because of his father's crimes, but others "had accepted him because he had distanced himself from that life".

"I hope the verdict would bring some comfort to those who had lost friends and relatives," Dan tells BBC's Newsday.

On Monday, Stephen Mwiti, 48, who said he had lost all six of his children to the cult, welcomed the verdict.

"I'm a happy man, that all persons have been convicted," he told the BBC outside court.

His former wife was one of those convicted of murder alongside Mackenzie.

Delivering her eight-hour judgment in the port city of Mombasa, Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece".

One of his co-accused told the court that Mackenzie had said anyone who resisted fasting must be forced to go to heaven "through kicks and blows".

Burials in the forest where the cult was based were described as "weddings", with those who died celebrated as having "wedded with Jesus", the judge said.

Mackenzie and other cult leaders also face separate cases involving terrorism, radicalisation and denying children an education.

The murder verdict is the first ruling on the most serious charges against the pastor, who was arrested in 2023 after more than 400 bodies were discovered in shallow graves in Shakahola forest, near Kenya's coast.

'I fear for my sons': Mother awaits DNA results on remains linked to Kenya's starvation cult

Go to BBCAfrica.com , external for more news from the African continent.

Follow us on Twitter @BBCAfrica , external , on Facebook at BBC Africa , external or on Instagram at bbcafrica , external

items.title: Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.cloudflare.com/typescript-rust-port/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50165953 Points: 130 # Comments: 73
items.content:
Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs , a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain .

Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building. Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser.

To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.

The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation. A Rust port has to follow those decisions closely, or it will eventually fall apart and become incompatible. We have to preserve the TypeScript language strictly based on its original implementation – and the TypeScript team should remain solely responsible for deciding what that looks like.

Early benchmarks of our Rust port of TypeScript are promising: tsrs is up to 8x faster and uses ~70% less memory compared to TypeScript 7.0 when using the same number of type check workers:

As you can see, the next version of TypeScript already brings many performance improvements, making TypeScript 7.1 beta up to 2.5x faster than TypeScript 7.0. Some of these optimizations were upstreamed from tsrs , and we’re hoping to find more.

You may have seen recent benchmarks of different TypeScript ports with various performance claims, often due to using larger machine types and different options compared to TypeScript’s defaults. We worked with the TypeScript team to ensure the above benchmarks are comparing the same configuration.

By default, tsrs ships with an adaptive configuration dependent on the machine type that uses more memory but is even faster:

TypeScript in Rust aims to be a faithful port of TypeScript. You can try an experimental release by installing the tsrs package from npm:

We’ve seen many attempts at porting TypeScript to other languages over the years. Because of the complexity involved, only one of the ports succeeded: the TypeScript team’s port of TypeScript from JavaScript to Go.

However, frontier AI models can now do large-scale ports almost independently in a matter of days. We have now seen slopforks, faithful ports, and completely re-architected versions of TypeScript in Rust or C++. There is clearly a demand for even faster TypeScript.

You might be thinking: “TypeScript’s Go port already made TypeScript 10x faster and far more memory efficient than the previous version written in TypeScript. Why isn’t that enough?”

However, it’s not just about speed. Rust offers some unique advantages: running in WebAssembly . The Rust + Wasm story has always been strong, and one of the reasons comes down to the fundamentals of Rust’s language design. When you compile a Go program to Wasm, you have to compile Go’s garbage collector along with it. But Rust’s memory management model enables straightforward memory interactions between a WebAssembly guest and host. This is one of the key things that makes Rust a much better fit for the WebAssembly use-case: memory efficiency.

Cloudflare Workers have supported Wasm for a long time. Just a few weeks ago we announced supporting native Rust in Workers with the new Emscripten target for wasm-bindgen. When you run entire software build and deployment systems in tight loops on Workers, the benefits of a small memory footprint pay off quickly. It means you can run these workloads so efficiently that it’s now possible to run fully encapsulated development systems in places where they couldn’t have been run before.

This enables new possibilities when combined with agents: You are now able to run a development toolchain end-to-end in a fully sandboxed environment on Cloudflare. But with Wasm, you can also run those environments safely client-side in your browser, or on an embedded device, or an IoT application.

First, we are working with Theo Browne to merge tsc-rs and tsrs into a single package that supports all of TypeScript’s features including Language Server Protocol (LSP) and content mappers. Second, we’ve seen a lot of success with how we maintain Vinext in sync with its upstream, Next.js. We explained how we do this in a recent blog post :

We will apply the same process to TypeScript, taking extreme care that we don’t introduce diverging behaviors from upstream TypeScript. When we come across performance improvements, we’ll attempt to contribute them back to the TypeScript Go codebase so everyone wins.

Finally, we recognize that there are some differences to the upstream version of TypeScript right now, like for example the order in which diagnostics are printed. We aim to reduce those differences to a minimum by the time we publish a stable release.

Cloudflare is already the home of many free and open source Rust tools that power the JavaScript ecosystem, such as Vite, Rolldown, Oxlint, and Oxfmt. With more than 10 million developers building on Cloudflare, we care a lot about making the underlying developer toolchain faster, more portable, and easier to run in more places. We are excited to experiment with deeper tsrs integrations into our stack, for example for type-aware lint rules in Oxlint.

Like with Vinext, our goal is to run tsrs as a well-maintained healthy open source project — without getting in the way of TypeScript itself. The Oxc team has already begun refactoring the codebase to make it faster, use less memory, and make it maintainable. We know the TypeScript team is taking this seriously – they are experimenting with memory and performance improvements for tsc . We are excited to collaborate with the TypeScript team and the JavaScript community to build the best and fastest implementations of TypeScript together.
